rubric_items.reason: With the implement step's tests, every branch of AppointmentService.get and every page-notice condition is tested. Gaps: S-2 AC2 (a started Scheduled appointment with an Inactive doctor) has no API test, and S-5 AC2/AC3 are claimed but not checked.

Most assertions check observable results: flag values, the doctor-page list, 404 status, notice order and DOM position. Weak spots: the S-4 close-response asserts cannot tell apart status logic, and history is only checked through its heading, with an empty history.

Covers the 51st appointment past the doctor-page cap, the local weekday across UTC midnight, the exact start instant and one minute after, Completed/No-show with an Inactive doctor, a stray flag on closed statuses, and the unknown-id 404.

API tests are in api/test and use Vitest, Supertest, the fixed clock and skipIf(!pgAvailable()). Web tests are in web/src/__tests__ and use Testing Library with a stubbed fetch. Every test name starts with HMS-13 REQ-n.
No test counts or coverage numbers are made up. Counts are left to checks.json, and the coverage skip matches the verifier (coverage step status skip, exit 78).

findings.text: S-2 AC2 (a started Scheduled appointment with an Inactive doctor still shows the Inactive notice) is not tested at the API level. Known maps S-2 only to the page test, and no new or existing test checks doctorStatus for an appointment that has already started.

cites.quote: Given a Scheduled appointment whose start time has already passed and whose doctor is Inactive
S-2: covered by the page test for the Inactive notice and its placement.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an API test: make a doctor Inactive, then GET a Scheduled appointment using a clock after its start, and assert doctorStatus INACTIVE with outsideAvailability false.

findings.text: The S-4 close-response asserts cannot fail. When complete and no-show run, doctor 2 is still Active and Monday 09:00-10:00 is inside its block, so outsideAvailability is false whatever the status. The artifact still says both the close responses and GET are covered.

cites.quote: toMatchObject({ status: 'COMPLETED', outsideAvailability: false })
put('/api/doctors/2/availability')
feePaise: 80000, slotMinutes: 30, availability: [{ weekday: 1, start: '09:00', end: '10:00' }]
both in the close responses and afterwards on GET

findings.suggested_fix: Move the availability change before the complete and no-show calls, or say that only the GET checks are meaningful.

findings.text: Known says S-5 is covered, but the REQ-9 page test only checks AC1. AC2 (page exactly as before when there is no notice) is not checked. History is only checked by waiting for its heading, using a fixture with an empty history.

cites.quote: S-5: covered by the page test checking that the details, actions and history are unchanged.
then the page shows exactly what it showed before this change.
cancellationReason: null, history: []
await screen.findByRole('heading', { name: 'History' });

findings.suggested_fix: Use a fixture with at least one history event and assert it renders. Add a no-notice test that checks the details, actions and history, or narrow the S-5 Known line to AC1.

findings.text: The API edge tests depend on running in order. The REQ-3 boundary test reads doctor 3's first appointment, which the AC5 test creates. The S-4 test avoids a clash with a booking made in the first test. Running one test alone breaks them.

cites.quote: get('/api/appointments?doctorId=3')).body.items[0]
Patient 1 already holds Monday 09:00 with doctor 1 (first test)

findings.suggested_fix: Have each test create the doctor or appointment it needs, or move the shared setup into beforeAll.
